historical_context.time_period: Low Sere's standing present; exact date, calendar, and wider chronology remain unresolved.
historical_context.location: The Upper Shelf at Low Sere: three fixture-bounded guest sheds, the trader road marker, a witness bench, and the track above the warm basin.
historical_context.summary: A travelling small-goods seller attempts the ordinary closing of a hosted stay. The paired return-shards do not fit, forcing traveller, sponsor, and water witness to choose among delay, amended passage, practical search, and departure without false closure.

public_facts.text: Low Sere depends on warm grey water from an old intake and uses its mineral ash for pottery, pigment, abrasive work, and trade.
The Upper Shelf holds guest sheds and the trader road marker; outsiders remain there until a household, work crew, or basin table accepts their water use and safe route out.
Kalsan travel depends on negotiated water, shelter, readable warnings, accepted threshold speech, and obligations carried by hosts.

ambient_pressures.text: Return-shards split one hosting claim between marker and traveller so neither party can privately close or rewrite it.
An open shard charges the guest's water use to the sponsor and obliges current warnings, a competent route description, or escort when road marks are unsafe.
A mismatch proves no crime, but it suspends new sponsorship until witnesses separate water, guidance, delay, and loss.
Low Sere's unequal basin-table standing means a visible custom can preserve disagreement without guaranteeing an equal hearing.

groups.label: Upper Shelf travellers and local sponsors
institutional_logic: Make temporary access to scarce water and a promised exit legible without treating hospitality as permanent jurisdiction.
material_incentives: Remain eligible to host or return
internal_virtues: Humor that leaves room for correction
internal_shames: Using departure pressure to force false closure
prestige_markers: A return-shard that fits after a difficult stay
A host who walks an unsafe mark
A traveller who leaves water and route accounts separable
taboo_triggers: Calling a mismatch proof of guilt
emotional_display_norms: Suspicion is compressed into object handling, route readback, practical jokes, and insistence that the pieces remain visible.
trust_defaults: Trusts matched fracture, witnessed custody, separate water accounting, and present route knowledge more than a smooth recollection.
speech_register_cues: Dry jokes about water and clay

groups.label: Low Sere water witnesses acting at the Upper Shelf
institutional_logic: Keep water use, sponsorship, route warning, and unresolved claims visible to the basin table without deciding motive from the marker.
material_incentives: Keep outsiders from disappearing into household accounts
Prevent sponsors from accumulating hidden claims
internal_virtues: A route repeated before it changes
No guilt inferred from pottery alone
internal_shames: A richer sponsor's memory replacing the break
An open claim lost in the marker
prestige_markers: Two halves kept apart until their relation is witnessed
Water settled even when route responsibility remains open
taboo_triggers: Breaking a substitute pair that silently overwrites an earlier obligation
emotional_display_norms: Concern appears as careful hands, literal sentences, patient obstruction, and jokes delivered without surrendering custody.
trust_defaults: Trusts the material state and separately attributed accounts; distrusts urgency presented as proof.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The pair exists because either host or traveller may later improve the story; dignity comes from putting the claim where both can contest it.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Give both parties practical reasons to hurry and equal permission to preserve the mismatch without turning mutual suspicion into constant hostility.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Cheap clay can keep an expensive water and route obligation open; the witness must make that cost visible without inventing guilt.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Let delay, extra water, escort, and sponsorship standing change outcomes while the cause of the mismatch remains unresolved.

observer_read: A person turning a missed departure into procedure
A local gatekeeper protecting the marker's dignity
target_self_read: A witness keeping water, route, custody, and motive from collapsing into one convenient account
misread_patterns: Treats literal custody as distrust of the person rather than distrust of unilateral memory
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep Sava's impatience legible while allowing Nemi's obstruction to protect Sava from a false closure too.

observer_read: People whose timetable invites them to merge distinct obligations
Two narrators each holding a useful half
target_self_read: A host and traveller trying to preserve work, route, reputation, and an ordinary relationship
misread_patterns: Can underweight missed trade or onward company
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep Nemi from treating procedure as costless or reading either person's urgency as guilt.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A hosted outsider who controls one shard half, needs an onward route, and can refuse false closure without owning the marker or local hearing.
obligations: Separate water settlement from route dispute
Choose whether departure is worth an open claim
failure_modes: Letting the timetable certify a substitute
Calling solitary departure a safe route

role_pressure_fields.summary: A Low Sere worker whose water allotment and standing carry the guest's use and promised exit until the pair closes.
obligations: Name or walk the promised route
Accept suspension while the claim remains open
failure_modes: Substituting a fresh shard for an unresolved claim
Using familiarity to take both halves

role_pressure_fields.summary: A local witness who compares pieces and accounts, keeps disputed custody visible, and routes unresolved claims to the basin table.
obligations: Infer no crime from a mismatch
failure_modes: Letting a powerful sponsor dominate the account
Allowing a replacement pair to erase the first

known_context.text: Sava knows the carried half, the water used, the route named at arrival, the approaching departure group, and what each person says in the scene.

beliefs.text: Sava believes a useful custom must preserve a refusal without making every delay into guilt.

misreads.text: Sava may read careful witness work as local attachment to procedure when it also protects the traveller's account.

must_not_know.text: Sava must not know who moved, lost, traded, or mismatched a half unless a branch discovers direct evidence.

known_context.text: Olan knows the water mark, sponsorship obligations, routes he can presently describe or escort, and whether the marker half matches his memory.

beliefs.text: Olan believes practical escort can preserve the relationship even when the marker fails to close it.

misreads.text: Olan may treat custody offered to him as trust when it also makes later attribution more difficult.

must_not_know.text: Olan must not know why the pieces differ merely because he sponsored the stay.

known_context.text: Nemi knows the marker's current sockets, the visible pieces, the guest-water account, the route terms stated in witness, and the basin-table path for an open claim.

beliefs.text: Nemi believes the ritual is useful only if a mismatch stays visible and motive stays undecided.

misreads.text: Nemi may underweight the material cost of Sava missing onward company.

must_not_know.text: Nemi must not infer guilt, intent, or a universal route law from the shard alone.

author_only_boundaries.text: Return-shards are a Low Sere elaboration, not a universal Kalsan road law, currency, language family, measure, or divine rite.
The phrase 'let the break remember' is an author-facing English rendering of local advice; it establishes no spelling, grammar, etymology, or mutual intelligibility.
The fixture's three named people, three-shed layout, departure group, and mismatched pieces are scene-bounded and do not become standing event canon.

open_questions.question: Who physically maintains and inventories the Upper Shelf marker across work-watches?
open_questions.notes: The elaboration uses an existing water witness or current guest-shed tender and does not found a separate office.

open_questions.question: How are travellers without a sponsor supplied, refused, redirected, or represented at Low Sere?
open_questions.notes: The owner note explicitly identifies unsponsored travellers as a failure edge; this fixture begins after sponsorship and does not settle it.

open_questions.question: Which wider trade routes and language affiliations connect Low Sere to neighboring settlements?
open_questions.notes: Both remain unresolved in the canonical place note. The fixture uses only the local shelf track, a high cut, and author-facing English.
